metadata.notes: daemon=full: parser.go accumulates PerTurnContribution from model_completed only (goal_usage_attribution's byte-identical duplicate is skipped); TestTokenAccounting_EndToEnd (ran green) proves non-double-counting + monotonic accumulation. No dollar cost persisted anywhere in muse's transcript (strict key scan); no muse pricing entry exists yet in core/pkg/capacity, so cost_nonzero will be false at record time -- a caveat, not a bug. driver=ready: the three defects that could have corrupted or blocked a recording (untrusted-workspace modal, dropped Enter, subagent-transcript misresolution) were fixed same-day in 0239a1bd, confirmed present in the current driver-interactive.sh.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full (cost is a caveat, not a daemon bug)
driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

### agent_supports: yes

Muse's own transcript (`session.jsonl`) carries real per-call token usage. `runtime.session` -> `kind:"run"` -> `event.kind:"model_completed"` fires once per LLM call and carries `usage{input_tokens,output_tokens,cached_tokens,cache_write_tokens,cache_read_tokens,reasoning_tokens}` plus `model` (muse-format-spec.md §6, live-captured example: `{"input_tokens":29356,"output_tokens":99,"cached_tokens":0,"cache_write_tokens":0,"cache_read_tokens":0,"reasoning_tokens":28}`). A second event, `goal_usage_attribution`, re-emits the SAME usage with ownership metadata (main vs. subagent) -- confirmed byte-identical to the paired model_completed usage in every real record checked (§6). The agent performs and durably records the multi-turn token accounting this scenario is about.

### daemon_capability: full

`core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go` (`parseModelCompleted`, lines ~367-419) reads `model_completed` and builds `ev.Contribution = &tailer.PerTurnContribution{Model, Usage: UsageBreakdown{Input, Output, CacheCreation5m, CacheRead}}` on every LLM call, which is what the tailer folds into `SessionMetrics`'s cumulative, monotonically non-decreasing token totals -- exactly the scenario's acceptance criterion (`TotalTokens > 0` after turn 1; non-decreasing after turn 2+). `goal_usage_attribution` is explicitly skipped (`case runEventGoalUsageAttribution: ev.Skip = true`, parser.go:277-279) with a package-doc citation explaining why: it never carries a model id and its usage numbers were directly compared, paired by run_id/adjacent sequence, and found byte-identical to model_completed's every time checked -- counting both would double-count.

I ran the adapter's own unit test to confirm this end-to-end rather than trust the source read alone: `go test ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/... -race -count=1` -> `ok` (1.3s). `TestTokenAccounting_EndToEnd` (metrics_test.go) drives a synthetic two-turn transcript containing BOTH model_completed and its goal_usage_attribution duplicate for turn 1 through the PRODUCTION `tailer.NewTranscriptTailer` and asserts `CumInputTokens`/`CumOutputTokens`/`CumCacheReadTokens` land at exactly the values model_completed alone implies -- proving the duplicate contributes nothing extra.

The fresh-input netting for a cached turn is also handled: `parseModelCompleted` computes `Input = nonNegative(input_tokens - cache_read_tokens)`, with `cached_tokens` as a fallback when `cache_read_tokens` is absent (the `--provider echo` shape). The doc comment states this was verified inclusive-not-additive across 476 real `model_completed` records with nonzero usage scanned from the live corpus on this machine (parser.go:377-390) -- input_tokens never once smaller than the cache count, and cached_tokens/cache_read_tokens were byte-identical in every one of those 476 records. Unlike mistral-vibe (whose sidecar exposes no cache field at all -- a genuine agent-side gap noted in that cell's own caveats), muse's parser DOES expose a distinct `CacheRead` bucket, so the scenario's third criterion (`CacheReadTokens > 0`, fresh input = 0 for a fully-cached turn) is structurally observable here, not an architectural gap.

**No dollar cost is persisted anywhere in muse's transcript** -- verified by a strict JSON-key scan (not a substring match) across all 48 session.jsonl/approval-review files in the corpus (muse-format-spec.md §6): zero records carry an actual key matching /cost/i; every earlier substring hit was toolset/instruction prose. The MSP wire schema defines a `ModelCost` type and a `session/tokenUsage` notification, but neither was found written to session.jsonl. This exactly matches the daemon's existing contract for every other adapter: cost is computed client-side from `model_id` against `core/pkg/capacity`'s pricing catalog. I confirmed no such catalog entry exists yet for any muse model (`git grep -in muse core/pkg/capacity/` -> zero hits), so `EstimatedCostUSD` will legitimately be 0 at record time -- `metrics_test.go`'s own comment documents this as the same gap mistral-vibe's Mistral models carry. Cost is NOT in the scenario's acceptance_criteria (only token counts and the cache bucket are), so per the caveats-over-downgrades rule this stays a caveat, not a daemon=bug.

`session-index.db` (the SQLite sidecar) has no token/usage/cost columns at all and is unreliably synced (2 of 14 sessions indexed at read time, one showing `status='missing_metadata'` for an actively-running 400+-record session) -- the adapter deliberately never reads it for metrics (adapter.go's package doc cites this explicitly); session.jsonl is the sole, sufficient source.

**Open item, not decided here**: `automated_review_completed` (the `:auto-review` LLM-judge's own review lifecycle, under `kind:"approval"`) may carry its own judge-call token usage -- real, currently-uncounted tokens (on the order of tens of thousands in a sampled session, per the concurrent research). `parseApprovalEvent`'s default arm (parser.go:534-543) skips this event entirely today -- confirmed by reading the switch. Whether judge-review tokens belong in session-level token accounting (a real cost the user's account pays) or are legitimately out of scope (an internal review sidecar, not the user-facing turn) is a product decision for the maintainer, not settled by this assessment.

### driver_capability: ready

The recipe is a 3-turn interactive REPL sequence (send -> wait_turn -> sleep, x3), needing `send`, `wait_turn`, `sleep`. `replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh` declares `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean"` (line 139) -- all three needed types are in the driver's own capability declaration, confirmed by reading the case-dispatch block directly (not just the constant). This driver was live-audited (muse-driver-audit.md) and found to have 3 critical + 2 lesser defects that would have blocked or silently corrupted any recording (untrusted-workspace modal eating the first prompt, a dropped Enter with no inter-keystroke delay, `resolve_transcript`'s `find|sort|tail -n1` landing on a subagent's transcript instead of the driven session's own, teardown never producing a clean session.end, and turn_count() swallowing jq read failures as \"zero turns\"). All five were fixed same-day in commit 0239a1bd (`fix(muse): repair the recording driver so it can't record a corrupted pass`) -- I confirmed the fixes are actually present in the current file, not just claimed in the commit message: `--trust-workspace` on the launch command (line 235), `sleep 0.3` between the text and Enter sends in `step_send`, `-not -path '*/subagent/*'` in `resolve_transcript`'s find (line 301), a real `step_exit_clean` sending `/exit` and polling for the process/session.end to settle (no longer stubbed), and `turn_count`/`step_wait_turn` distinguishing a read failure (`EXIT_REASON=\"nonzero(4)\"`) from a genuine zero-turns timeout.

## Route

agent=yes + daemon=full + driver=ready -> **record**: proceed straight to a live recording.
caveats: No dollar cost is persisted anywhere in muse's transcript (verified: strict JSON-key scan across 48 corpus files finds zero /cost/i keys, muse-format-spec.md §6). Cost computes client-side from core/pkg/capacity, and no muse model has a pricing entry there yet (git grep confirms zero hits) -- so cost_nonzero will read false at record time. Not in the scenario's acceptance_criteria, so this is a caveat, not a daemon bug.

OPEN ITEM for the maintainer, not decided here: automated_review_completed (the :auto-review LLM-judge's own review lifecycle) appears to carry its own judge-call token usage that the parser currently never reads (parseApprovalEvent's default arm skips it, parser.go:534-543). Whether those judge tokens should fold into session-level accounting is a product decision, out of scope for this assessment.

PROVISIONAL on live emission: daemon=full here rests on reading parser.go plus a SYNTHETIC end-to-end unit test (TestTokenAccounting_EndToEnd, confirmed green by running it). Whether a REAL 3-turn live session actually produces the expected cache-read pattern on turn 2/3 (muse's own prompt-caching behavior, not directly tested live here) is settled only by record's live recording.

The scenario's 'fully cached turn -> fresh input tokens = 0' sub-criterion has no metric form in the phase DSL (same documented limitation as the claudecode sibling spec) -- it is asserted via the observation vector / caveats, not a phase. Whether any live turn nets to EXACTLY zero fresh input (vs. a small nonzero remainder from the new prompt text itself) is uncertain until record's live recording; muse's parser does expose a distinct cache_read bucket structurally, unlike mistral-vibe which has none at all.

Model pinned as muse-spark-1.3-contributor from live corpus evidence (muse-format-spec.md §7: run.model.configured / runtime.model_reconfigure.completed, consistent across all 16 sessions inspected on this machine), not from vendor docs. This is tied to the 'meta'/'tbh' provider/profile default on this account -- record should reconfirm it's still current.

session-index.db carries no token/usage/cost columns and is unreliably synced (2 of 14 sessions indexed, one showing status='missing_metadata' for an active session) -- the adapter correctly never reads it for metrics; noted so a future auditor doesn't wonder why no sqlitero sidecar read exists here.

Driver fixes (commit 0239a1bd) are same-day and confirmed present in the file by direct reading, but not yet proven by an actual completed recording run -- record is what turns 'grammar/semantic-verified' into battle-tested.

Vacuous-pass check: this cell would pass while proving nothing if the recorded session's 3 turns produced zero token usage (e.g. a provider/account misconfiguration silently degrading to --provider echo, which the live corpus shows omits cache_read_tokens/cache_write_tokens entirely) -- record must confirm nonzero Contribution.Usage on each of the 3 turns, not just 3 clean ready<->working cycles.

sources.note: parseModelCompleted (~L367-419): builds PerTurnContribution from model_completed's usage, netting cache_read_tokens out of input_tokens (476-sample verification cited in the doc comment); goal_usage_attribution explicitly Skip=true (L277-279) as model_completed's confirmed-duplicate.

TestTokenAccounting_EndToEnd: ran `go test ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/... -race -count=1` myself (ok, 1.3s) -- synthetic 2-turn transcript including a goal_usage_attribution duplicate of turn 1, asserts CumInputTokens/CumOutputTokens/CumCacheReadTokens reflect model_completed ONLY.
git grep -in muse core/pkg/capacity/ -> zero hits: no pricing entry for any muse model yet, so EstimatedCostUSD is legitimately 0 at record time.

§6 Token + cost accounting: live-captured model_completed/goal_usage_attribution examples, the strict cost-key scan finding zero results, and session-index.db's schema/sync-gap evidence. §7 for the live-verified model id.
Live-reproduced (tmux) evidence for the 3 critical + 2 lesser driver defects, each with a before/after repro.

DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean" (L139); confirmed --trust-workspace (L235), sleep 0.3 in step_send, -not -path subagent exclusion in resolve_transcript (L301), and step_exit_clean/turn_count fail-loud fixes are present in the current file, not just the commit message.
fix(muse): repair the recording driver so it can't record a corrupted pass -- same-day fix for all 5 driver defects the audit found.
Template for the 3-turn single-birth recipe/spec shape (send/wait_turn/sleep x3, birth anchored unpinned to start).
Sibling cell precedent for the cost/cache caveat phrasing and the route derivation from the 3 pillars.

preconditions: muse CLI installed and on PATH (muse --version >= 1.2.1), and authenticated (muse login / META_API_KEY, per replaydata/agents/muse/metadata.json)
irrlichd is recording (--attach against a daemon started with --record, or isolated/coexist mode -- muse has no compiled-in adapter on the production release yet)
PID binding is via the session's own .session.lock file (pid.go's DiscoverPID), not a CWD-based election, so a concurrent unrelated muse session elsewhere does not interfere
driver-interactive.sh's 0239a1bd fixes are in place: --trust-workspace at launch, the sleep 0.3 send/Enter gap, and resolve_transcript's subagent/ exclusion -- all confirmed present
setup: Driver launches muse in a fresh cwd under <staging>/cwd/ with --trust-workspace (skips the untrusted-workspace modal)
No special model or context flags -- default model is fine; the assertion is about token accumulation and cache-read behavior across turns, not which model produced the tokens

SessionMetrics.TotalTokens after turn 2 >= TotalTokens after turn 1 (monotonic)
